title: Pregnancy & Antenatal Care
excerpt: Regular check-ups, scans and guidance from early pregnancy until delivery.
seo_description: Regular check-ups, scans and guidance from early pregnancy until delivery. Dr. Jawaria Rasheed, consultant gynecologist.

settings.editor: Antenatal care means regular check-ups during pregnancy to look after the health of the mother and baby. Good care helps identify problems early and prepares you for a safe delivery.

icon_list.text: You have a positive pregnancy test
You are planning a pregnancy and want advice beforehand
You had complications in a previous pregnancy
You have diabetes, high blood pressure, thyroid or another condition

settings.editor:
• Confirmation of pregnancy and expected due date
  • Routine blood tests and ultrasound scans at the right stages
  • Blood pressure, weight and baby’s growth checks
  • Advice on diet, supplements, activity and warning signs
  • Planning for delivery, with referral where needed

Most check-ups are monthly in early pregnancy and become more frequent towards the end. Your schedule will be adjusted to your health and your baby’s needs.

When to seek urgent care: Contact a hospital emergency department straight away if you have heavy bleeding, severe abdominal pain, fits, severe headache with blurred vision, leaking fluid, or your baby’s movements reduce.

icon_list.text: Confirmation of pregnancy and expected due date
Routine blood tests and ultrasound scans at the right stages
Blood pressure, weight and baby’s growth checks
Advice on diet, supplements, activity and warning signs

tabs.tab_title: When should I have my first antenatal visit?
tabs.tab_content: Ideally soon after a positive pregnancy test, usually in the first 8–10 weeks.

tabs.tab_title: Which supplements should I take?
tabs.tab_content: Folic acid is usually advised before and in early pregnancy. Your doctor will advise on iron, calcium and other supplements based on your tests.

title: Infertility Evaluation
excerpt: A step-by-step assessment for couples who are trying to conceive.
seo_description: A step-by-step assessment for couples who are trying to conceive. Dr. Jawaria Rasheed, consultant gynecologist.

settings.editor: If you have been trying to conceive without success, a fertility evaluation looks for possible reasons in both partners. Understanding the cause is the first step towards the right treatment.

icon_list.text: No pregnancy after 12 months of regular, unprotected intercourse
After 6 months if the woman is 35 or older
Irregular or absent periods
Known PCOS, endometriosis, or previous pelvic surgery or infection
Repeated miscarriages

settings.editor:
• A detailed history for both partners
  • Hormone blood tests and an ultrasound scan
  • Tracking of ovulation
  • Semen analysis for the male partner
  • Tests of the fallopian tubes where needed
  • A personalised plan explained in plain language

Fertility is a shared concern — about a third of cases involve the male partner. Coming together to the consultation helps us plan quickly and avoid unnecessary tests.

icon_list.text: A detailed history for both partners
Hormone blood tests and an ultrasound scan
Tracking of ovulation
Semen analysis for the male partner

tabs.tab_content: It is very helpful. Male factors are common, and a semen test is simple and important.

tabs.tab_title: Is every couple offered IUI?
tabs.tab_content: No. Treatment depends on the results. Some couples need only ovulation support or lifestyle changes. Others are referred for IVF when that is the better option.

title: IUI (Intrauterine Insemination)
excerpt: A simple fertility treatment that places prepared sperm directly into the uterus at the time of ovulation.
seo_description: A simple fertility treatment that places prepared sperm directly into the uterus at the time of ovulation. Dr. Jawaria Rasheed, consultant gynecologist.

settings.editor: Intrauterine insemination (IUI) is a fertility treatment in which washed and prepared sperm are placed inside the uterus around the time of ovulation. It brings the sperm closer to the egg and is less invasive than IVF.

icon_list.text: Unexplained infertility
Mild male factor (slightly low count or movement)
Ovulation problems such as PCOS, together with ovulation medicines
Problems with cervical mucus
Difficulties with intercourse

settings.editor:
• Ovulation is monitored by ultrasound, often with medicine to support egg growth
  • A trigger injection may be given to time ovulation
  • The partner’s semen sample is washed and prepared in the lab
  • The sperm are placed into the uterus with a thin, soft catheter — it takes a few minutes and is usually painless
  • A pregnancy test about two weeks later

IUI needs at least one open fallopian tube and healthy enough sperm, so these are checked first. Success varies with age, the cause of infertility and other factors. Several cycles may be needed, and your doctor will discuss realistic expectations and when to consider other options.

icon_list.text: Ovulation is monitored by ultrasound, often with medicine to support egg growth
A trigger injection may be given to time ovulation
The partner’s semen sample is washed and prepared in the lab
The sperm are placed into the uterus with a thin, soft catheter — it takes a few minutes and is usually painless

tabs.tab_title: Is IUI painful?
tabs.tab_content: Most women feel little or no pain — it is similar to a Pap smear. Mild cramps for a short time are possible.

tabs.tab_title: Can I go back to normal activities afterwards?
tabs.tab_content: Yes. Most women return to normal daily activities the same day.

tabs.tab_title: How many IUI cycles are advised?
tabs.tab_content: This depends on your age and test results. Your doctor will review progress after each cycle and advise when another approach may be better.

title: Ovulation Induction & Follicle Monitoring
excerpt: Medicines and ultrasound tracking to help regular, well-timed ovulation.
seo_description: Medicines and ultrasound tracking to help regular, well-timed ovulation. Dr. Jawaria Rasheed, consultant gynecologist.

settings.editor: Ovulation induction uses medicines to help the ovaries release an egg. Follicle monitoring (follicular tracking) uses ultrasound scans to follow how the egg is growing, so that intercourse or IUI can be timed correctly.

icon_list.text: Irregular or absent ovulation, for example with PCOS
Before or together with IUI
Unexplained infertility

settings.editor:
• Tablets or injections at the start of your cycle
  • Several short ultrasound scans to measure follicle growth
  • Advice on the best days to try to conceive
  • Careful dose adjustment to lower the chance of multiple eggs

Monitoring makes treatment safer. It shows when the egg is ready and helps avoid over-response of the ovaries.

tabs.tab_content: Usually two to four scans in a cycle, a few days apart, depending on how the follicles grow.

title: PCOS Care
excerpt: Diagnosis and long-term management of polycystic ovary syndrome.
seo_description: Diagnosis and long-term management of polycystic ovary syndrome. Dr. Jawaria Rasheed, consultant gynecologist.

settings.editor: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is a common hormonal condition. It can cause irregular periods, acne, extra hair growth, weight gain and difficulty getting pregnant. With the right plan, symptoms can be well controlled.

icon_list.text: Periods that are irregular, infrequent or absent
Acne or unwanted facial or body hair
Difficulty losing weight
Trouble conceiving

settings.editor:
• Diagnosis based on symptoms, blood tests and ultrasound
  • Checks for related risks such as blood sugar and cholesterol
  • Lifestyle guidance that is realistic for you
  • Treatment to regulate periods, manage symptoms or support ovulation

PCOS is a long-term condition, but it is manageable. Even modest weight loss, when appropriate, can improve periods and fertility. Your plan will match your goals — whether that is regular periods, clearer skin or pregnancy.

icon_list.text: Diagnosis based on symptoms, blood tests and ultrasound
Checks for related risks such as blood sugar and cholesterol
Lifestyle guidance that is realistic for you
Treatment to regulate periods, manage symptoms or support ovulation

tabs.tab_title: Can women with PCOS get pregnant?
tabs.tab_content: Yes, many do — sometimes naturally and sometimes with help such as ovulation induction.

title: Period Problems
excerpt: Help for heavy, painful, irregular or missed periods.
seo_description: Help for heavy, painful, irregular or missed periods. Dr. Jawaria Rasheed, consultant gynecologist.

settings.editor: Periods that are very heavy, painful, irregular or missed are common, but they are not something you simply have to live with. Finding the cause allows effective treatment.

icon_list.text: Bleeding that soaks through pads quickly or lasts more than 7 days
Pain that stops you from daily activities
Cycles shorter than 21 or longer than 35 days
Bleeding between periods or after intercourse
Bleeding after menopause

settings.editor:
• Questions about your cycle (a period diary helps)
  • Blood tests, for example for anaemia and thyroid
  • Pelvic ultrasound

title: FAQs
seo_description: Answers to common questions about appointments, IUI and women’s health care with Dr. Jawaria Rasheed.

settings.editor: Answers to common questions about appointments and care.

tabs.tab_title: How do I book an appointment?
tabs.tab_content: Use the online request form, call the clinic or send a WhatsApp message. The clinic will confirm your date and time.

tabs.tab_title: Is my appointment confirmed when I submit the form?
tabs.tab_content: Not yet. The form sends a request. Your appointment is confirmed when the clinic contacts you.

tabs.tab_title: Can my husband or a family member come with me?
tabs.tab_content: Yes. For fertility consultations it is especially helpful if both partners attend.

tabs.tab_title: What should I bring to my first visit?
tabs.tab_content: Previous reports and scans, a list of your medicines and the date of your last period.

tabs.tab_title: Is IUI the same as IVF?
tabs.tab_content: No. In IUI, prepared sperm are placed in the uterus and fertilisation happens naturally inside the body. In IVF, eggs are collected and fertilised in a laboratory. IUI is simpler and less invasive. IVF may be advised in other situations.

tabs.tab_title: Are consultations private?
tabs.tab_content: Yes. Your concerns are discussed confidentially, and examinations are done only with your consent.

tabs.tab_title: Do you provide emergency care?
tabs.tab_content: No. For heavy bleeding, severe pain or other emergencies, please go to the nearest hospital emergency department.
